why: Leg 1 passes: the sentence exists verbatim at line 33 of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/skills.md, and the rest of that line ('Pass "all" ... or [] to disable all. When you set `skills`, the SDK adds the Skill tool to `allowedTools` automatically.') does not reverse it. Leg 2 half-fails: the named function does not exist. `grep -rn buildClaudeSessionOptions` over packages/ and apps/ returns nothing; the real helper is `buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions` (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:272-308), and the cited :301 is the closing brace of its systemPrompt literal. Its own doc comment says it is a three-option SLICE ('The turn-shape SDK options Nessy passes explicitly ... Extracted from chatImpl's inline options object so the three shapes are testable'), NOT the session options object. `settingSources: ['user','project','local']` at :305 and the absence of `skills` are both real. Leg 3 refutes the finding: the actual Options object is assembled at claude-agent.ts:1213-1630 and one layer down it disables the SDK skill mechanism outright. :1118 `const disallowedTools: string[] = ['EnterPlanMode','ExitPlanMode','AskUserQuestion','Skill'];`, wired in at :1626, and :1629 `plugins: []` carrying the comment at :1627-1628 'No plugins — skills are handled by BaseAgent.chat() via read-before-execute (the model reads SKILL.md files directly, enforced by PrerequisiteManager)'. The installed SDK typings define the effect precisely (node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.d.ts:1303-1307): disallowedTools tools 'will be removed from the model's context and cannot be used, even if they would otherwise be allowed.' So the SDK Skill tool is absent from every Claude-backend turn and no SDK-discovered SKILL.md is invocable. The claimed consequence — 'every SKILL.md under ~/.claude/skills/ and <cwd>/.claude/skills/ is enabled ... chosen by the SDK rather than by Nessy's capability resolver' — is therefore false: Nessy's resolver (BaseAgent.buildPinnedCapabilityContext / capabilityTurnRuntime.view, materializeRuntimeSkillInvocation, PrerequisiteManager) is the only skill path that reaches the model, exactly as intended. This is also the repo's documented sibling-subsystem trap: the live `Skill` handling at pre-tool-use.ts:134/1435 and SessionManager.ts:964 is Nessy's OWN skill tool name, not the SDK's discovered-skill tool. Not one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (that list's skill row is `SkillMetadata.disallowedTools`, an unrelated frontmatter field) — it is simply an implemented architectural choice, not an inert contract.
correctedState: buildClaudeTurnShapeOptions (packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:272-308) is a deliberate three-option slice of the turn options, not the whole session options; the claim's function name buildClaudeSessionOptions does not exist. It is true that `skills` is never passed and that settingSources is ['user','project','local'], so the SDK still DISCOVERS user/project skills. But the Claude backend then removes the SDK's Skill tool from the model's context (claude-agent.ts:1118 -> :1626, disallowedTools) and passes plugins: [], because skills are served exclusively by Nessy's capability resolver via read-before-execute (BaseAgent.buildPinnedCapabilityContext / capabilityTurnRuntime.view, materializeRuntimeSkillInvocation, PrerequisiteManager). Nessy therefore has ONE authoritative skill-gating system on the Claude path, not two; the resolver's enabled:false policy is not bypassed. The only residual, unverified and cosmetic, is whether the SDK still spends context listing discovered skill names when the Skill tool is removed; passing skills: [] would settle that as belt-and-braces context hygiene, but it changes no gating behaviour.
